metadata.description: Comprehensive consumer spending patterns, income, debt, payment methods, and economic behavior for 5 countries. All data from 2022+ unless noted as historical benchmark.
sources: DOSM Malaysia Household Income & Expenditure Survey 2022
Banca d'Italia Household Income and Wealth Survey 2022

dataPoints.context: Urban Indonesian households allocate 45.5% of monthly expenditure to food; rural households allocate ~55%. National average tilts toward food-heavy spending.
Non-food expenditure (housing, transport, education, health, clothing) represents 54.5% of urban household spending in Indonesia.
As of February 2024, the average Indonesian employee earns ~IDR 3 million/month net (~USD 190). Urban workers earn 20-30% more than rural.
Jakarta 2024 monthly minimum wage IDR 5,067,381 (~USD 316). In 2023 it was IDR 4,641,854. Among highest provincial minimums in Indonesia.
Employees aged 55-59 in Indonesia earn ~IDR 3.9 million/month. Peak earning years are mid-career (35-49).
Indonesia Gini ratio reached 0.388 in March 2023, the highest since September 2018. Urban inequality is rising faster than rural.
84.3% of Indonesian e-commerce users used e-wallets (OVO, GoPay, DANA, ShopeePay) as primary payment method in 2023.
Bank transfers accounted for 30.2% of total e-commerce payment value in Indonesia in 2023, second after e-wallets.
Over 10% of e-commerce purchases in Indonesia were still made using cash on delivery in 2023, reflecting large unbanked population.
71% of Indonesian digital wallet users have used GoPay; 58% are loyal recurring users. GoPay tied with OVO for top position.
70% of Indonesian digital wallet users have used OVO; 53% used it in the last 3 months in 2023 surveys.
~50% of 16-24 year old Indonesians spend IDR 50,000-100,000 per food delivery order (~USD 3-6). GoFood led with 75% usage in 2023.
75% of Indonesian food delivery app users stated GoFood (Gojek) was the app they used most in 2023.
During Ramadan 2023, food & beverage spending rose 8.3% YoY. Clothing sales rose 8.4%. THR (religious holiday bonus) drives 82% to spend on clothing, 75% on food.
Ramadan is Indonesia's biggest retail window. In 2022, grocery/gift spending during Ramadan was ~8% higher than rest of year; 2022 grew 9% over 2021.
Jakarta 1-bedroom apartment city center: USD 170-360/month. Bali equivalent is USD 680-1,050/month (64% more expensive than Jakarta).
A typical meal at a local warung or inexpensive restaurant in Indonesia costs ~USD 1.78 for lunch/dinner. Breakfast ~USD 1.18.
Public transport in Indonesia costs ~USD 0.25 per ride. Monthly public transport pass ~USD 12.
Remittances to Indonesia grew ~6% to reach USD 10 billion in 2022. Remittances received = ~1.1% of GDP in 2024.
Indonesia annual household expenditure per capita reached USD 1,143 in 2023. Very low by global standards, reflecting large rural/informal economy.
Tipping is not culturally expected in Indonesia. Service charges (10%) are added at upscale restaurants. Warung and street food require no tip.
Housing (rent, mortgage services) is the largest Australian household expense at AUD 254 billion nationally in 2023, representing ~21% of total household expenditure.
Food accounted for AUD 117 billion of Australia's national household spending in 2023. About 10% of total household expenditure.
Recreation and culture is Australia's second biggest spending category at AUD 123 billion in 2023, reflecting high discretionary spending culture.
Median weekly earnings in May 2023: AUD 1,300 all employees, AUD 1,509 males, AUD 1,130 females.
dataPoints.source: ABS Employee Earnings and Hours May 2023

dataPoints.context: Peak earning years in Australia: age 35-44, median full-time weekly salary AUD 1,821 (~AUD 94,700/year). Age 15-19 earns AUD 800/week full-time.
Australia household savings ratio bottomed at 1.8% in June 2023 quarter — lowest in 16 years. High mortgage payments depleted household savings during RBA rate hike cycle.
Average Australian household debt was AUD 261,492 (~USD 175K) as of December 2022. Total national household debt: AUD 2.6 trillion — 4th highest in OECD.
Total Australian housing debt: AUD 2,288.3 billion in December 2022, up from AUD 530.9 billion 20 years prior. Almost entirely driven by housing finance.
20% annual surge in credit demand in Q1 2023. 10% increase in debts >90 days overdue. Combined credit card balance fell 38% Jan 2020 to Jun 2022 low, then rebounded.
Debit cards accounted for 57.9% of total purchase value in 2022, up from 32.3% in 2002. Three-quarters of card transactions now debit over credit.
Australia Gini coefficient 0.32 — equal 20th highest among 35 OECD countries, exactly at OECD average of 0.32.
~25% of Australians now tip after a meal. Tipping is voluntary, not expected. ~10% is norm when given. High minimum wage removes necessity to tip.
Typical tipping rate in Australia is 10% when given, at fine dining or exceptional service. Eftpos machines increasingly prompt for tips, causing cultural shift since 2021.
1-bedroom apartment city center in Sydney: ~AUD 2,800/month (vs ~AUD 2,106 in Melbourne). Sydney rent is ~29% higher than Melbourne.
A flat white coffee in Australia averages AUD 5.00-6.00. Australia has a strong specialty coffee culture, especially Melbourne. Third wave coffee predominant.
Meal at inexpensive restaurant in Australia averages AUD 20-25. Mid-range restaurant 3-course for 2: AUD 90-110.
Average Christmas gift spending per person in 2023: AUD 646, down from AUD 700 in 2022. Cost-of-living pressures reduced discretionary holiday spending.
Australia's pre-Christmas retail sales hit record AUD 66.8 billion in 2022. In 2023 forecast was ~AUD 67 billion with only 0.1% growth YoY.
dataPoints.source: Roy Morgan / ARA Christmas Retail Sales 2022/2023

dataPoints.context: Australians planned to spend AUD 434 on average at Black Friday sales 2023, the biggest single sale event. Boxing Day average: AUD 370.
Sydney monthly public transport spend is highest in Australia — nearly double that of Adelaide. Opal card with capped daily spending.
Average monthly Italian household expenditure was EUR 2,738 in 2023, up 4.3% nominal from EUR 2,625 in 2022. Real terms fell 1.5% due to inflation.
Italian households spend EUR 289/month on transport on average in 2023. This includes car ownership, public transport, and fuel costs.
Italy Gini index was 33.7 in 2022, up from 32.8 in 2020. Income inequality rising post-pandemic. South Italy significantly more unequal than North.
Italian households saved ~7% of disposable income in Q4 2022. However, over 50% of all households saved nothing in 2022. Rises to 70% for lowest income quintile.
More than 52% of Italian households saved nothing in 2022. For lowest income quintile: 70% saved nothing. Top quintile: only 28% saved nothing.
26% of Italian households held debt in 2022, stable from prior year. Top half of income distribution held 85% of total loans from financial institutions.
Cash was used for ~44% of transactions in Italy in the early 2020s — one of the highest in Western Europe. Italy remains a cash-heavy society despite digitalization.
Credit cards are the most common e-commerce payment method in Italy — 37% of Italian e-commerce companies accept them. Digital wallets: 27%.
PayPal holds 91% market share among digital wallets in Italy. Digital wallets (PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay) used for ~38% of online purchases.
Italy average household income EUR 38,700/year, slightly above OECD average of EUR 38,300. However, net disposable income varies heavily by region (North vs South).
Tipping is not obligatory in Italy. When given, typically small amounts — rounding up or leaving 1-2 EUR. Cash preferred for tips. Service charge (coperto) often already added.
Cappuccino at Italian bar: EUR 1.20-1.80. Typical Roman breakfast (cappuccino + cornetto): EUR 2.50-3.50 at local bar. Espresso ~EUR 1.20.
dataPoints.source: Expat cost of living sources Italy 2023

dataPoints.context: Meal at Italian trattoria/inexpensive restaurant: EUR 10-15. 3-course mid-range restaurant for 2: EUR 50-80. Milan tends to be 30-40% more expensive than Rome.
1-bedroom apartment in Milan city center: EUR 1,200-1,700/month. Rome is cheaper: EUR 900-1,300. Milan is Italy's most expensive city for housing.
Rome public transport (100-minute ticket): EUR 1.50. Day ticket: EUR 7.00. Milan 90-minute ticket: EUR 2.20. Public transport used widely but car ownership high.
Holiday spending in Italy shrank over 10% in 2022 due to inflation. Italy has official winter sales starting January (saldi invernali) and summer sales in July.
Italy e-commerce revenue was estimated at EUR 76 billion in 2022. Online purchases forecast EUR 54.2 billion in 2023 by some measures (different scope).
65% of Italian shoppers actively hunt for discounts (up from 58% in 2023), reflecting persistent price sensitivity from 2022-2023 inflation period.
dataPoints.source: Rome Business School / Retail Trends Italy 2024

dataPoints.context: 82% of Singapore households made online purchases in 2022/23 HES, up from 60% in 2017/18. Online now represents 11.9% of monthly household expenditure.
Online purchases represent 11.9% of Singapore households' monthly expenditure on average in 2022/23.
Median monthly income of full-time employed residents in Singapore: SGD 5,197 in 2023 (up from SGD 5,070 in 2022). Real income fell 2.2% after inflation.
dataPoints.source: MOM Singapore Gross Monthly Income Survey 2023

dataPoints.context: Median Singapore salary for age 20-24: SGD 2,800. Biggest jump occurs at 25-29 (+SGD 1,218, +43.5%). Salaries peak at age 45-49 at SGD 6,487.
Singapore median salary peaks in the early 40s at SGD 6,458 (age 40-44) to SGD 6,487 (age 45-49). Post-50 salaries decline as many transition roles.
Bottom 10% of Singapore households: avg monthly income per member = SGD 706. Top 10%: SGD 14,803. Massive 21x spread reveals concentrated wealth.
Top 10% of Singapore households earn SGD 14,803 per member per month vs SGD 706 for bottom 10% — a 21x ratio in a high-cost city-state.
Singapore Gini coefficient after taxes and transfers: 0.35 in 2023. Before transfers it is significantly higher, reflecting government redistributive policies.
Singapore gross national savings rate: 47.2% of GDP — one of the highest in the world. Driven by CPF mandatory savings system, high incomes, and cultural thrift.
84% of Singaporean food delivery app users stated GrabFood was the app they used most in 2023. Grab dominates with largest GMV share.
dataPoints.source: Statista Singapore Favorite Food Delivery Apps 2023

dataPoints.context: Singaporeans spend an average of SGD 118/month on food delivery platforms. Majority spend SGD 10-30 per order. 60% order at least once a week.
60% of Singaporeans order food delivery at least once per week (Deliveroo study). 22% order 1-2 times per week. Zero switching cost between apps leads to multi-app behavior.
Hawker center meal in Singapore: SGD 5-10. Mid-range restaurant: SGD 30-80 per person. Hawker centers are cultural institution and primary budget dining.
Monthly public transport spend in Singapore: SGD 120-160. MRT/bus system covers entire island. Concession cards for students and elderly reduce cost significantly.
1-bedroom apartment in Singapore city center: SGD 2,500-4,000/month in 2023. Outskirts: SGD 1,500-2,500. Housing is the dominant household expense.
Tipping is NOT expected in Singapore. Fine dining adds 10% service charge automatically. Hawker centers: no service charge. PayNow/GrabPay widely accepted everywhere including hawkers.
Upscale, casual dining in CBD/Orchard, hotel restaurants, seafood restaurants add 10% service charge + 9% GST. Hawker centers and kopitiams: no service charge.
dataPoints.source: Don Signature Crab / Tipping in Singapore guides 2023

dataPoints.context: Singapore is highly cashless. PayNow (bank-linked), GrabPay, DBS PayLah! used widely. Even hawker centers and taxis accept digital payments. MAS reports near-universal adoption.
Singapore housing loan non-performing loan (NPL) ratio: 0.2% as of Q2 2023 — very low. Other individual loans NPL: 0.6%. Household debt quality remains healthy.
Singapore online food delivery market size: USD 621.78 million in 2023. ~3 million Singaporeans ordered food online in 2022.
Average Malaysian household spent MYR 5,150/month in 2022. Expenditure grew faster than incomes, partly financed by EPF withdrawals and government aid.
dataPoints.source: DOSM Malaysia Household Expenditure Survey Report 2022

dataPoints.context: Housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels = 23.2% of Malaysian household expenditure in 2022, the largest single category.
Food and non-alcoholic beverages = 16.3% of Malaysian household expenditure. Combined with restaurant & accommodation (16.1%), total food-related = ~32.4%.
Restaurant & accommodation services = 16.1% of household expenditure in Malaysia 2022. High eating-out culture in Malaysia driven by affordable hawker/mamak stalls.
Transport = 11.3% of Malaysian household expenditure in 2022. High car ownership driven by limited public transport outside KL and Penang.
Average Malaysian household income: MYR 8,479/month in 2022 (up 2.4% from MYR 7,901 in 2019). Median income: MYR 6,338/month (+2.5%/year).
Malaysian median household income: MYR 6,338/month in 2022 vs MYR 5,873 in 2019. Growth of 2.5%/year. Median is more representative than average given inequality.
Malaysia e-commerce reached MYR 135.7 billion in 2022. Strong growth driven by Shopee, Lazada, and local platforms.
Cash remains the most preferred payment mode in Malaysia at 41% in 2023. Debit card second (~18%), e-wallets third (~14%).
~90% of Malaysian consumers surveyed used Touch 'n Go eWallet in the past 3 months in 2023. TNG holds 62% preference. Accepted at 2+ million merchants.
93% of Malaysian e-wallet users committed to continued use regardless of incentives in 2023, showing organic adoption beyond promotional drives.
Malaysia's shadow economy accounts for ~21% of GDP (~MYR 330 billion). Lower than 2000-2009 period (30.2%). Shadow economy shrinking due to TIN system and e-invoicing.
Malaysia had ~2.22 million registered migrant workers in 2022 (12.9% of total employment). Major source countries: Indonesia, Bangladesh, Nepal, Myanmar.

Hari Raya Aidilfitri is Malaysia's biggest retail event — 60% of population is Muslim. Spending surges on clothing, cooking ingredients, and home goods. March 2025 retail jumped 6.6% YoY driven by pre-Raya spending.
Meal at inexpensive restaurant in KL: MYR 10-20 (~USD 2-5). 3-course mid-range for 2: MYR 100 (~USD 23). Mamak stalls are 24-hour staple at MYR 7-12.
1-bedroom apartment in KL city center: MYR 1,500-2,500/month (~USD 330-550). Suburbs: MYR 800-1,500/month. Very affordable vs regional peers.
KL public transport starts at MYR 1.50 (USD ~0.30) for one station. Range based on distance. LRT, MRT, KTM Komuter. Car ownership high due to limited coverage outside KL.
Malaysia had 7.9 million households in 2022, with average 3.8 members per household. Urban households (72%) skew higher income.
Tipping is not standard in Malaysia. Fine dining may include 10% service charge + 6% SST. Hawker stalls, mamak restaurants: no tipping expected.
The four main expenditure groups (housing+utilities 23.2%, food 16.3%, restaurants 16.1%, transport 11.3%) account for 66.9% of all Malaysian household spending.
Indonesia food delivery GMV reached USD 4.5 billion in 2022. Grab had 49% share, Gojek 44%. Market expected to grow to USD 33.2 million revenue by 2027.
Australian household expenditure reached AUD 1.19 trillion in 2023 (slightly under AUD 1.2 trillion in 2022). Transport spending surged +35.8% in Nov 2022 YoY.
Singapore daily commuters without car: roughly SGD 40-50/month on public transport. Singapore has world-class MRT/bus system with EZ-Link card.
dataPoints.source: Expat cost sources / Singapore transit authorities 2023

dataPoints.context: 82% of Malaysian consumers spend their Hari Raya budget on clothing (new baju Raya/kurung), making fashion the top Raya category. 75% also spend on food & beverages.
99% of Indonesian Ramadan shoppers prioritize affordability above brand loyalty. Price sensitivity is dominant even during biggest spending period of year.
Indonesia's annual household expenditure per capita was USD 1,135.68 in Dec 2024, nearly unchanged from USD 1,143.44 in 2023. Extremely low by ASEAN standards.
Hotels, cafes and restaurants accounted for AUD 88 billion of Australian household spending in 2023. Hospitality surged post-COVID but softened in H2 2023.
Insurance and other services: AUD 93 billion in 2023 household spending. Insurance costs rising significantly with inflation and climate risk in Australia.
Ferragosto (August 15) triggers massive domestic travel and tourism spend. Rome/Venice/Florence see huge visitor surges. Restaurants/hotels see peak revenue. Many businesses close entire August.
dataPoints.source: Travel And Tour World / Italy cultural calendar 2023

dataPoints.context: Chinese New Year is Singapore's biggest retail event (75% ethnic Chinese population). Spending surges on gifts, ang pow (red packets), new clothes, food and travel. Major retailers offer Lunar New Year sales.

Malaysia has 4 major retail seasons: Christmas/year-end (Nov-Dec), Chinese New Year (Jan-Feb), Hari Raya (Mar-May depending on year), and Deepavali (Oct-Nov). Effectively continuous festive retail calendar.
dataPoints.source: iMoney Malaysia / PUNB Malaysia festive analysis 2023

dataPoints.context: Cards (debit + credit) accounted for 17.4% of Indonesia e-commerce transaction value in 2023. Well below regional peers due to lower banking penetration.
Australia's shadow/informal economy estimated at ~9-10% of GDP. Much lower than Southeast Asian peers. Tax compliance high due to ATO enforcement and digital payments.
Singapore is one of Asia's top luxury goods markets per capita. High income, zero import tax on most luxury goods, and tourist shopping make it a luxury hub. Major brands maintain flagship stores.
dataPoints.source: Bain & Co Luxury Study 2023 / industry data

dataPoints.context: ~7.5% of Italians experience material deprivation including food insecurity. Southern Italy significantly worse than North. Energy costs in 2022-23 squeezed poorest households most.
Myanmar workers in Malaysia sent USD 211.58 million in remittances in Nov 2022 - Apr 2023 (6 months). Total Malaysia remittance outflows estimated at several billion USD annually.
Indonesian urban middle class spends ~45% on food + housing (necessities). Remaining 55% covers transport, education, health, and discretionary. Limited luxury spending outside Jakarta top 10%.
~30% of Australian consumers used Buy Now Pay Later (Afterpay, Zip, Klarna) in 2022-2023. Australia pioneered BNPL adoption globally. Regulation increased in 2023.
CPF (Central Provident Fund): employees contribute 20% of wages, employers contribute 17% (for under 55). Total 37% of wages mandatorily saved for retirement/housing/health.
Italy household debt to disposable income ratio ~70% — well below EU average (~95%). Italian households historically conservative with debt. Low mortgage penetration vs Northern Europe.
dataPoints.source: Banca d'Italia / ECB Household Finance Survey 2022

dataPoints.context: Traditional kopi (coffee) at kopitiam: SGD 1.20-2.00. Specialty cafe coffee: SGD 6-9. Two-tier coffee culture: budget traditional vs premium specialty.
Kopi-O / teh tarik at Malaysian mamak stall: MYR 2-4 (~USD 0.50-1.00). Premium cafe coffee: MYR 12-18. Mamak culture (24/7 Indian-Muslim eateries) is central to Malaysian daily life.
Specialty coffee (Kopi Kenangan, Fore, Starbucks) in Jakarta: IDR 30,000-65,000 (~USD 2-4). Local kopi tubruk at warung: IDR 5,000-10,000. Specialty coffee market booming among urban youth.
Online retail accounts for ~17-18% of total Australian retail sales in 2023. Post-COVID normalization (peaked ~19% in 2020-21). Dominant categories: apparel, electronics, home goods.
dataPoints.source: ABS / NAB Online Retail Sales Index 2023

dataPoints.context: E-commerce accounts for ~12% of total retail in Italy in 2023 — lower than EU average due to older demographics, preference for local shops, and persistent cash culture.
Online retail in Malaysia accounts for ~22% of total retail in 2022. Shopee and Lazada dominate. Hari Raya and 11.11 are peak online shopping dates.
Online retail accounts for ~24% of total retail spending in Indonesia in 2023. Tokopedia (Tiktok Shop merger), Shopee, and Lazada are top platforms. Social commerce growing fast.
Online purchases = 11.9% of monthly household expenditure per SingStat HES 2022/23. Total e-commerce penetration ~23% of retail. Amazon, Shopee, Lazada, Qoo10 dominant.
Indonesian households allocate ~5.8% of expenditure to health. JKN (universal health insurance) has expanded coverage but out-of-pocket spending remains significant for middle class.
dataPoints.source: BPS Susenas 2023 / WHO Indonesia Health Account

dataPoints.context: Education spending = ~6.2% of Indonesian household expenditure. Private tutoring (les) and private schools are significant cost for urban middle class families.
Average HECS-HELP (student loan) debt in Australia: ~AUD 23,680 in 2023. No interest but indexed to CPI. 2023 indexation of 7.1% sparked political backlash.
Student loans are not common in Italy. University fees are heavily subsidized (EUR 900-4,000/year for public unis). Family support is the primary funding mechanism. No student loan culture.
dataPoints.source: Italian Ministry of Education / OECD Education at a Glance 2023

dataPoints.context: Singapore government tuition grant (Singaporeans): ~SGD 21,000 for local public university. Students who take CPF Education Loan repay at 2.5% interest. Total debt manageable vs income.
PTPTN (national student loan) average debt: ~MYR 35,000 per graduate. ~4.7 million active borrowers. High default rate (~20%) is major government fiscal issue.
~28% of Australian mortgage holders were in 'mortgage stress' (spending >30% of income on mortgage) in 2023 due to RBA rate hikes from 0.1% to 4.35%.
~40% of Indonesian urban youth use 'paylater' (BNPL) services via Shopee PayLater, GoPay Later, Akulaku. High default rates reported; labeled a 'debt trap' by financial authorities.
Malaysia household debt-to-GDP ratio ~90% — among highest in Southeast Asia. Mostly housing loans. Bank Negara Malaysia monitors closely for systemic risk.
dataPoints.source: Bank Negara Malaysia Financial Stability Report 2022

dataPoints.context: 78% of Singaporeans live in HDB (public housing) flats. Housing relatively affordable via CPF OA savings for down payments. Private property market is ultra-premium.
74% of Italian households own their home — one of the highest in EU. Cultural norm to own property. Low mortgage debt partly because homes passed down through generations.
Sydney median house price ~AUD 1.2 million in 2023 (recovered after 2022 dip). Melbourne: ~AUD 780,000. Australia has some of the world's highest house-price-to-income ratios.
Singapore GST (Goods and Services Tax) rose to 9% in 2024 (from 8% in 2023, 7% before 2023). Affects all consumer prices. Government offsets impact via vouchers for lower-income households.
Malaysia SST (Sales & Service Tax) increased from 6% to 8% for services in 2024. Food and basic necessities exempted. Affects restaurant bills and services.
Indonesia PPN (VAT) rate is 11% since April 2022 (up from 10%). Basic food commodities are exempt. Plan to increase to 12% was paused in 2024.
Australia GST is 10% (unchanged since 2000). Fresh food, healthcare, education exempt. This is relatively low vs EU/Singapore. No state income tax.
Italy IVA (VAT) standard rate: 22%. Reduced rates: 10% (food, tourism, some transport) and 4% (basic foods, books). One of EU's highest headline VAT rates.
Singapore food delivery market ~SGD 826 million in 2023 (USD 621.78M). Population 5.9 million. Per capita food delivery spend among world's highest at ~SGD 140/capita/year.
dataPoints.source: Mordor Intelligence / Taiwan News Singapore Food Delivery 2023

dataPoints.context: Malaysia food delivery market ~MYR 5.8 billion in 2023. GrabFood and FoodPanda are dominant. Shopee Food grew rapidly then exited in 2022. Strong adoption in KL and Penang.
~59% of Indonesian workers are in informal employment (2023 BPS data). Informal workers have lower and more volatile incomes, limited access to banking, more reliant on cash.
Malaysia informal employment: ~27% of workforce. Includes hawker stalls, unlicensed traders, gig workers. Shadow economy = ~21% of GDP.
Australia food delivery market ~AUD 4.2 billion in 2023. Uber Eats leads with ~50% share, DoorDash second. High delivery fees (AUD 3-8) limit frequent use vs Southeast Asia.
dataPoints.source: Roy Morgan / Statista Australia Food Delivery 2023

dataPoints.context: Italy food delivery market ~EUR 1.8 billion in 2023. Just Eat (now part of Takeaway), Deliveroo, Glovo are main players. Adoption lower than Northern Europe due to strong restaurant/pizza delivery culture.
dataPoints.source: Statista / Mordor Intelligence Italy Food Delivery 2023

dataPoints.context: Singapore receives minimal remittances (~0.2% GDP). It is primarily a remittance SENDER country. Foreign workers send significant sums to Philippines, India, Bangladesh, China.
Australia sends ~AUD 4.3 billion in remittances annually (World Bank 2022). Large immigrant communities from India, China, Philippines, UK. Second-largest remittance source in Pacific region.
Indonesian households allocate ~4.2% of expenditure to clothing. Spikes during Ramadan/Eid (Lebaran) when 82% of consumers buy new clothes. Muslim fashion (hijab) is a major market.
Australian household clothing and footwear spending ~AUD 32 billion annually (2022). Category experienced -0.8% decline in Christmas 2023 as cost-of-living pressures bit.

Italian households spend ~6.5% of budget on clothing and footwear — higher than EU average, reflecting Italy's strong fashion culture. January and July official saldi (sales) drive concentrated spending.
Healthcare out-of-pocket spending = ~7% of Singapore household expenditure. Medishield Life provides catastrophic insurance. High-quality private healthcare available at premium.
Malaysian households spend ~8.1% on education. High demand for private schools and tuition centres especially among Chinese Malaysian families. Education is cultural priority.
Private health spending in Australia = ~3.3% of GDP. Medicare covers public health but 45% of Australians hold private health insurance (~AUD 2,400-4,800/year per family).
68% of Italians shop during official saldi (summer/winter sales). July and January are two biggest clothing purchase months. Sales season culturally embedded.
Great Singapore Sale and year-end Orchard Road sales drive retail peaks. Average spend per shopper during major sale events: ~SGD 485. Tourism multiplies retail spending.
dataPoints.source: STB Singapore Tourism Board / Retail industry data 2022

dataPoints.context: Chinese Malaysian households spend ~MYR 2,500 on Chinese New Year (ang pow, new clothes, food, decorations, travel). Chinese Malaysians = ~22% of population.
THR (Tunjangan Hari Raya) is mandatory by law: employees receive 1 month salary bonus before Eid al-Fitr. This concentrates massive consumer spending in April-May window.
dataPoints.source: Ministry of Manpower Indonesia / Annual THR regulation

dataPoints.context: Easter is Australia's second-biggest retail event after Christmas. ~AUD 1.2 billion spent on Easter-related items (chocolate, travel, food). Retail seasonality: Christmas > Easter > Mother's Day > Father's Day.
dataPoints.source: ARA Australia Retail Sales / Roy Morgan 2023

dataPoints.context: International tourists to Singapore spend avg SGD 1,200 on shopping per trip (2023). Singapore is duty-free hub with major luxury flagships. Tourism-driven retail = significant GDP contribution.
44% of Italians planned to shop Black Friday 2023, up from 38% in 2022. American retail events increasingly adopted in Italy, especially for electronics and fashion.
Malaysia 11.11 (Singles Day) online spending grew ~35% YoY in 2022. Shopee 11.11 is the biggest online shopping event of the year, surpassing Hari Raya in digital channels.
Indonesia 11.11 (Singles Day) online spending grew ~25% YoY in 2022. Shopee, Tokopedia, and Lazada all record massive GMV peaks. Social commerce via TikTok Shop growing.
Australia's top remittance destinations: India, China, Philippines, UK, NZ. Total outflows ~USD 4.3 billion. High migrant population (28% born overseas) drives strong remittance flows.
dataPoints.source: World Bank KNOMAD / ABS Migration Data 2022

dataPoints.context: Singapore remittance outflows ~SGD 8.1 billion annually. Top destinations: Philippines, India, Bangladesh, Indonesia, China. Significant portion via informal channels (hawala) for lower-skilled workers.

Italy sends ~EUR 7.9 billion in remittances annually. Large immigrant communities (Romanian, Albanian, Moroccan, Chinese, Filipino) send money home. Italy is one of Europe's largest remittance senders.
dataPoints.source: Banca d'Italia / World Bank Italy Remittances 2022

dataPoints.context: Singapore households spend ~8.5% on recreation and entertainment. Casinos (Marina Bay Sands, RWS), concerts, theme parks, sports events. High disposable income enables strong entertainment spend.
Australia spends ~AUD 25 billion/year on gambling — highest per capita in the world. Poker machines (pokies), sports betting, horse racing. Significant drag on lower-income household budgets.
dataPoints.source: ACIL Allen / Australian Institute of Health and Welfare 2022

dataPoints.context: ~70% of Italian meals are home-cooked (vs ~45% in Singapore). Strong food culture prioritizes fresh local ingredients. Supermarket spending on quality ingredients is cultural norm.
Malaysia's petrol subsidy costs MYR 14.4 billion in 2023. RON95 petrol kept at MYR 2.05/litre — far below market price. Subsidy rationalization began 2024 for higher-income groups.
Indonesia fuel and energy subsidies reached IDR 551 trillion in 2022 — massive cost to keep Pertalite fuel at IDR 10,000/litre. Key factor keeping transport costs artificially low.
Australian households spend ~AUD 1,200/month on food (groceries + dining out). Coles and Woolworths (Duopoly) control ~65% of grocery market — persistent complaint about high food prices.
dataPoints.source: ABS Household Expenditure / ACCC Supermarkets Inquiry 2023

dataPoints.context: Singapore households spend ~SGD 1,200/month on food (hawker + restaurants + groceries). Food is second-largest household expense after housing. Hawker centers subsidize food costs.
Malaysian households spend ~MYR 1,670/month on food (groceries + restaurants = ~32.4% of MYR 5,150 avg). Affordable hawker and mamak culture keeps food costs low.
Italian households spend ~EUR 575/month on food and beverages at home + restaurants. Food quality is paramount — premium olive oil, wine, cheese, cured meats drive higher spend.
Indonesia luxury goods market ~USD 1.9 billion in 2023. Concentrated in Jakarta upper class. Louis Vuitton, Hermes, Rolex in Pondok Indah Mall. Small but growing segment.
Australia luxury goods market ~AUD 7.8 billion in 2023. Premium wine, fashion, watches, vehicles. Sydney and Melbourne have full luxury retail ecosystems.
Singapore luxury goods market ~SGD 5.2 billion in 2023 for a population of 5.9M — extremely high per capita. Tourism + local HNWIs + zero import duty = luxury hub.
Italy domestic luxury market ~EUR 20 billion in 2023. Italy is the world's #2 luxury PRODUCER (after France) — Gucci, Prada, Versace, Ferrari based here. Domestic consumption and tourism-driven.
Malaysia luxury goods market ~MYR 4.1 billion in 2023. Pavilion KL is the luxury retail hub. Strong Chinese-Malaysian high income segment drives luxury watch and brand spending.
Only 51.8% of Indonesian adults have formal bank accounts (2022 World Bank Findex). Large unbanked population relies on e-wallets as first financial product (GoPay, OVO).
88% of Malaysian adults have formal bank accounts (2022 World Bank Findex). High financial inclusion relative to income level. Islamic finance (takaful, Islamic mortgage) widely used.
98%+ of Singapore adults have bank accounts. Near-universal financial inclusion. Multiple bank accounts common. Digital banking (Trust Bank, GXS) disrupting traditional banking.
dataPoints.source: World Bank Global Findex / MAS Singapore 2022

dataPoints.context: 99%+ of Australian adults have bank accounts. Among world's highest financial inclusion rates. Digital banking via CBA, NAB, ANZ, Westpac and neobanks (Ubank, Up) widely used.
93% of Italian adults have bank accounts. Lower than Western European peers. Cash-heavy culture means some unbanked even in affluent regions. South Italy lower inclusion.
Australia has one of world's highest contactless payment adoption rates: 95% of card transactions are contactless. Pioneered tap-to-pay globally. Cash rarely needed.
Italian contactless payments grew 22% YoY in 2022, accelerating adoption but from low base. COVID accelerated cashless. Cash still at 44% of transactions — EU mandated cash acceptance.
PayNow processed ~SGD 9.8 billion/month in 2023, representing a fundamental shift from cash to instant bank transfers. Used for everything from hawker meals to rent.
QRIS (national QR payment standard) reached 26.9 million accepting merchants by end 2023. Unified QR enables cross-wallet payment — major digital payment infrastructure leap.
DuitNow QR is Malaysia's national QR payment standard (equivalent to Indonesia's QRIS). Accepted across all major banks and e-wallets. Malaysia-Singapore cross-border QR payment launched 2023.
42% of Australians aged 18-35 use BNPL services (Afterpay, Zip, Klarna) in 2023. Afterpay has 3.4 million active Australian customers. BNPL regulation introduced in 2023.
Singapore Certificate of Entitlement (COE) for a car reached SGD 97,000-106,000 in 2023 (for Cat B >1600cc). This makes Singapore cars 4-5x more expensive than same models elsewhere.
Italy has 65 cars per 100 people — highest in EU (EU avg ~45). Car culture very strong despite poor public transport outside cities. High transport costs reflect maintenance, fuel, insurance.
Indonesia has ~135 million registered motorbikes vs ~20 million cars (2023). Motorbike is primary household vehicle. Gojek/Grab ojek (motorbike taxi) apps transformed urban mobility.
~93% of Malaysian households own at least one car (2022). Driven by Proton/Perodua national car affordability, poor public transport outside KL, and subsidized petrol. High consumer auto loan debt.
dataPoints.source: DOSM Malaysia / MAA Malaysia Automotive Association 2022

dataPoints.context: Average Singapore household monthly expenditure: SGD 5,931 in 2023. Top 3 categories (housing SGD 2,122, food SGD 1,422, transport SGD 951) = 63.2% of all spending.
Singapore average monthly housing expenditure: SGD 2,122 in 2023. Includes mortgage repayments, HDB rent imputation, conservancy charges, utilities.
Singapore average monthly food expenditure: SGD 1,422 in 2023. 67.9% of food spending on food services (hawkers, restaurants, cafes), 32.1% on groceries.
Singapore average monthly transport expenditure: SGD 951 in 2023, down from SGD 1,038 in 2017/18. Private road transport fell from SGD 762 to SGD 678. Car costs very high (COE).
Singapore average monthly health expenditure: SGD 474 in 2023. MediShield Life covers catastrophic illness. Rising out-of-pocket costs for specialists and private care.
Singapore average monthly education expenditure: SGD 404 in 2023. Driven by private tuition (SGD 1.8 billion total industry). Richest households spend SGD 162+/month on tuition alone.
Singapore average monthly recreation, sport, and culture expenditure: SGD 335 in 2023. High entertainment spending reflects affluent, urbanized population.
Singapore private tuition industry: SGD 1.8 billion in 2023. Reflects intense academic competition in highly meritocratic system. Even hawker families spend on tuition.
dataPoints.source: Malay Mail / SingStat 2025 reporting on 2023 data

dataPoints.context: Low and middle income Australian households spend 18-19% of income on food vs 14% for high income households (2015-16 HES, still directionally valid). Food stress rising in 2022-23.
dataPoints.source: ABS Household Expenditure Survey 2015-16 / ACCC Supermarkets Inquiry 2023

dataPoints.context: Australians aged 25-29 spent AUD 955/month on essentials in 2023 (-3.7% YoY) and AUD 1,300 on discretionary (-6.2%). Cost pressures squeezing young adults hardest.
dataPoints.source: Budget Direct Australia Cost of Living Survey 2024

dataPoints.context: Average Australian household spends AUD 272/week on groceries (~AUD 1,178/month). Coles and Woolworths control ~65% of market. ACCC investigated pricing practices in 2023.
Italian households allocate 19.3% of total spending to food and non-alcoholic beverages — above EU average. Premium quality food is cultural norm; fresh markets preferred over supermarkets.
Italian households spend ~7.4% on health (OECD average). Italy has universal NHS (SSN) but out-of-pocket costs rising due to long public waiting lists. Private healthcare used by middle class.
Recreation and culture = ~8.3% of Italian household spending (OECD data). Italy's rich cultural heritage (museums, opera, football) drives recreation spending. Summer vacation is non-negotiable.
Malaysian workers aged 35-44 had median monthly salary of MYR 3,371 in 2024, up from MYR 2,865 in 2023. Peak earning bracket in Malaysia labor market.
dataPoints.source: DOSM Malaysia Salaries and Wages Survey 2024

dataPoints.context: Malaysian urban workers: mean monthly salary MYR 3,796 in 2024. Rural workers: MYR 2,847. Urban-rural wage gap = 33.3%, reflecting development disparity between KL and rural states.
Malaysian urban household median income: MYR 8,139 in 2024, up from MYR 7,243 in 2022 (+5.8%/year). Rural median: MYR 4,588 — 44% lower than urban.
Malaysian rural household median income: MYR 4,094 in 2022, up to MYR 4,588 in 2024. Rural areas concentrate B40 (bottom 40%) income group. Significant urban-rural income divide.
Indonesian urban casual workers aged 25-54: ~IDR 1.8 million/month (~USD 112) as of February 2023. Casual/informal workers earn far below formal employees.
Indonesian rural casual workers aged 25-54: ~IDR 1.62 million/month (~USD 101) as of February 2024. Rural wages ~10% below urban casual wages. Subsistence farming supplements income.
Indonesian rural self-employed aged 25-54: ~IDR 1.81 million/month in August 2023. Slightly higher than rural casual workers. Dominated by micro-trade, farming, fishing.
TikTok Shop Indonesia grew ~300% YoY in GMV in 2022-2023 before government regulation forced separation from TikTok app. After merger with Tokopedia (GoTo), relaunched as Tokopedia+.
Average Australian household electricity bill: ~AUD 2,200/year in 2023 (up 20-25% from 2022). Energy costs became major affordability issue. Government rebates partially offset increases.
Italian household energy (gas + electricity) spend peaked at ~EUR 298/month in early 2023 from 2022 energy crisis. Government capped bills via social bonus scheme for low-income.

Singapore average monthly utilities (electricity + water): ~SGD 165 for 4-room HDB flat in 2023. Electricity tariff rose 20%+ in 2022-23 due to global gas prices. Efficient buildings offset some cost.
dataPoints.source: SP Group / HDB Singapore utility data 2023

dataPoints.context: Malaysian household average monthly utility bill (electricity + water): ~MYR 180. TNB electricity tariff heavily subsidized. Malaysia has some of lowest domestic electricity prices in ASEAN.
Indonesian household average monthly electricity + water: ~IDR 350,000 (~USD 22). PLN electricity is subsidized for lower voltage users (450VA, 900VA). Unsubsidized rate ~2x higher.
Australian family private health insurance (hospital + extras cover): AUD 3,500-5,000/year. ~45% of Australians hold private health insurance, partly driven by Medicare Levy Surcharge avoidance.
dataPoints.source: APRA Private Health Insurance Data 2023 / AIHW

dataPoints.context: Average Australian household spends ~AUD 52/month on streaming subscriptions (Netflix, Stan, Disney+, Spotify, Amazon). Subscription fatigue growing in 2023 with cost-of-living pressures.
67.9% of Singapore food spending goes to food services (hawkers, restaurants, cafes). Only 32.1% on groceries. Eating out is effectively the default — hawker centers make this affordable.
Malaysia national median monthly salary: MYR 2,793 in 2024 (all occupations, all sectors). Mean salary: MYR 3,500+. Lower than household income due to multi-earner households.
dataPoints.source: DOSM Malaysia Salaries & Wages Survey 2024 / Human Resources Online

dataPoints.context: Southern Italian households spend ~35% less than northern counterparts. Southern regions (Campania, Calabria, Sicily) have significantly lower income, higher unemployment, and weaker purchasing power.

68% of Italians aged 18-34 still live with parents — highest in EU. High housing costs, precarious employment, and cultural norms explain 'mammismo'. Significantly reduces independent household formation.
Singapore top personal income tax rate: 24% (for income >SGD 1 million). Effective rates much lower. Combined with CPF, total tax burden still competitive vs OECD. No capital gains tax.
Australian average earner (AUD 80K) pays ~23% effective income tax including Medicare Levy (2%). Stage 3 tax cuts from July 2024 reduced burden for middle earners.
Italy top marginal income tax rate (IRPEF): 43% for income >EUR 50,000. Plus regional/municipal surcharges of 1.23-3.33%. High tax wedge discourages formal employment and drives shadow economy.
Malaysia top personal income tax rate: 30% for income >MYR 2 million. Most middle-income earners pay 8-24%. No inheritance tax, no capital gains tax on most assets.
Indonesia top personal income tax rate: 35% for income >IDR 5 billion/year (2023). Most workers in IDR 60-250 million bracket pay 5-15%. Low compliance in informal sector.
Indonesia digital banking users reached ~70 million in 2023. BRI, BCA, Mandiri lead digital. Neo-banks (Jenius, Blu, SeaBank) grew 40%+ YoY. Financial inclusion via mobile key strategy.
87% of Australians use mobile or internet banking regularly in 2023. CBA has highest digital adoption. Physical bank branch closures accelerating — 400+ closed in 2022-23.
Singapore CPI peaked at 6.1% YoY in September 2022, then eased to 2.7% by end 2023. Food inflation hit 7.5% in early 2023. Cost-of-living became top political issue.
Australia CPI peaked at 7.8% in December 2022 quarter — highest in 32 years. Food inflation peaked at 9.2%. RBA raised rates from 0.1% to 4.35% in 12 rate hikes, severely impacting mortgagors.
Italy HICP inflation peaked at 11.8% in October 2022 — highest since 1984. Energy drove most of increase. Food inflation +13%. Real household income fell sharply, reducing purchasing power.
Indonesia CPI peaked at 5.95% in September 2022. Fuel subsidy removal partially reversed in 2022 to control fiscal deficit. Food inflation was primary concern for low-income families.
Malaysia CPI peaked at 4.7% in August 2022. Lower than regional peers due to extensive price controls and subsidies (fuel, cooking oil, electricity). Subsidy rationalization in 2023-24.
dataPoints.source: DOSM Malaysia CPI 2022 / Bank Negara Malaysia

dataPoints.context: Indonesia smartphone penetration: 73% of population in 2023. 5th largest smartphone market globally. Mobile-first digital economy — most internet users never experienced desktop-first web.
dataPoints.source: Statista / We Are Social Indonesia Digital 2023

dataPoints.context: Malaysia smartphone penetration: 89% of population in 2023. High by Southeast Asian standards. Drives mobile commerce, food delivery, and e-wallet adoption.
dataPoints.source: We Are Social / Hootsuite Malaysia Digital 2023

dataPoints.context: Australia smartphone penetration: 91% in 2023. Mobile payments, food delivery, banking, shopping all heavily mobile-driven. Android and iOS evenly split.
dataPoints.source: We Are Social / Statista Australia Digital 2023

dataPoints.context: Italy smartphone penetration: 80% in 2023. Lower than Northern European peers due to older demographic skew. Mobile commerce growing but desktop still significant for purchases.
dataPoints.source: We Are Social / AGCOM Italy Digital 2023

dataPoints.context: Singapore smartphone penetration: 93% in 2023 — among world's highest. Fully mobile-first economy. 5G coverage near-universal. Digital government services via Singpass heavily used.
dataPoints.source: We Are Social / IMDA Singapore Digital 2023

dataPoints.context: Bali 1-bedroom central villa/apartment: USD 680-1,050/month. Bali is 64% more expensive than Jakarta for foreigners. Digital nomad demand drives premium prices vs local wages.
dataPoints.source: Bali.com / Numbeo Bali cost of living 2023

dataPoints.context: Singapore receives only ~USD 198 million in remittances (2022 World Bank). Negligible vs outflow of USD 6 billion+. As high-income city-state, Singapore is net sender not receiver.
55% of Italian food purchases happen in modern retail (supermarkets, hypermarkets). 30% in traditional/local markets. Remaining 15% in discounters (Lidl, Aldi gaining share rapidly).
Coles + Woolworths control 65% of Australian grocery market. ACCC 2023-24 Inquiry found evidence of potential pricing issues. Aldi (12%) and IGA (7%) are main alternatives.
65% of Indonesian consumer goods are still purchased in traditional markets (pasar tradisional) and warungs. Modern retail (Alfamart, Indomaret, hypermarkets) accounts for 35%.
Malaysia has ~10,000 convenience stores (7-Eleven: 2,700+, Mydin, KK Super Mart, Family Mart). High-density convenience store culture especially for urban grab-and-go food purchases.
35% of Singapore households regularly use online grocery delivery (RedMart/Lazada Fresh, FairPrice Online, Cold Storage). High cost of living makes time-saving services viable.
Italian households spend ~EUR 350/year on wine — world's highest per capita wine consumption. Wine is considered food staple, not luxury. Everyday table wine ~EUR 3-8/bottle.
dataPoints.source: Unione Italiana Vini / IWSR Italy Wine Report 2022

dataPoints.context: Australian households spend ~AUD 1,560/year on alcohol. Beer and wine are dominant. High alcohol excise tax makes Australia one of world's most expensive countries for alcohol.
Indonesia halal food market: USD 135 billion in 2022 — world's largest. 87% Muslim population drives universal halal certification requirement. Halal certification affects all food supply chain.
dataPoints.source: Dinar Standard / GIFR Global Islamic Finance Report 2022

dataPoints.context: Malaysia halal food and beverage market: ~USD 46 billion in 2022. Malaysia is global halal hub — JAKIM certification internationally recognized. Halal export target: USD 7.6 billion by 2025.
Indonesia internet penetration: 78.19% (2023) — 212 million users. Mobile internet dominant (95% mobile). Low latency urban broadband expanding but rural connectivity remains challenge.
Social commerce (TikTok Shop, Instagram Shopping) grew 42% in Australia in 2023. Particularly strong for beauty, fashion, home goods targeting Millennials/Gen Z.
Singapore hawker meal prices rose ~40% over the decade to 2023. Average hawker meal: SGD 5-10 in 2023 vs SGD 3-6 in 2013. Government hawker stall rental subsidies help maintain accessibility.
dataPoints.source: SFA Singapore Food Agency / media reports 2023

dataPoints.context: Malaysia food CPI rose 6.2% in 2023. Cooking oil, chicken, egg shortages in 2022 triggered panic buying. Price controls on essential goods (cooking oil, chicken, eggs, sugar) maintained throughout.
dataPoints.source: DOSM Malaysia CPI / Ministry of Trade 2022-2023

dataPoints.context: Indonesia cooking oil price spiked to IDR 25,000/litre in early 2022 (normally ~IDR 14,000). Government imposed price cap and export ban on palm oil. Drove food inflation and social unrest.
dataPoints.source: BPS Indonesia / Ministry of Trade Indonesia 2022

dataPoints.context: Singapore seniors (60+) receiving SG vouchers (Seniors' Bonus up to SGD 1,400) use them primarily at NTUC FairPrice, hawker centers, and pharmacies. Health and transport dominate elderly spending.
dataPoints.source: Singapore Ministry of Finance / Budget 2023 analysis

dataPoints.context: ANZ-Roy Morgan Consumer Confidence index averaged 78.5 in 2023 (below 100 neutral). Persistent pessimism driven by rate hikes, cost of living. Weakest sustained confidence in 35 years.
Bank Indonesia Consumer Confidence Index averaged 127.1 in 2023 (above 100 = optimistic). Indonesian consumers remain optimistic driven by strong domestic growth, employment, and Ramadan.
Malaysia MIER Consumer Sentiment Index: 82 in H2 2023. Below neutral (100). Sticky inflation and cost-of-living concerns weigh on Malaysian consumer outlook despite economic growth.
dataPoints.source: MIER Malaysia Institute of Economic Research 2023

dataPoints.context: Italy consumer confidence index: 96.1 in Q4 2023 (Istat, base 2010=100). Improved from lows of 90 in early 2023 as energy prices eased. Still below 100 neutral.
Household goods (furniture, appliances) spending: AUD 68 billion in 2022. Surged during COVID-19 nesting, then fell as RBA rate hikes slowed home improvement spending in 2023.
dataPoints.source: ABS Household Expenditure / ABS Retail Trade 2022

dataPoints.context: Australia annual pet spending: AUD 13 billion in 2023. One of highest pet ownership rates globally (69% of households). Pet humanization trend drives premium food, vet care, and accessories.
dataPoints.source: Animal Medicines Australia Pet Ownership Report 2022

dataPoints.context: Italian domestic tourism spending (vacations within Italy): ~EUR 94 billion in 2023. Summer beach and winter ski vacations are cultural mandatory spending. Ferragosto peak period.
dataPoints.source: ISTAT Tourism / Banca d'Italia Tourism Statistics 2023

dataPoints.context: Average Italian household spends ~EUR 1,850 on annual vacation. Summer (July-August) is near-universal vacation period. 'Ferie di agosto' means businesses close en masse.
Singapore household overseas travel spending: ~SGD 5,400/year per household (2023). Strong travel culture — Changi Airport processes 58 million passengers. Thailand, Japan, Bali top destinations.
Malaysian household annual domestic travel spending: ~MYR 3,200. Tourism Malaysia's Visit Malaysia campaigns drive domestic travel. Langkawi, Genting, Cameron Highlands top domestic destinations.
dataPoints.source: Tourism Malaysia / Bank Negara Annual Report 2022

dataPoints.context: Mudik (Lebaran homecoming travel): ~IDR 2.5 million average spend per household for transport, food, gifts. ~100 million Indonesians travel during Eid — world's largest annual migration.
Australian overseas travel spending: AUD 42 billion in 2023 (post-COVID recovery). Indonesia (Bali), UK, USA top destinations. Strong travel culture — 11 million departures in 2023.
Italian home improvement (renovation, maintenance) spending: EUR 64 billion in 2022. Superbonus 110% tax incentive drove record renovation spending in 2021-2023.
Malaysian household monthly telecom spend (mobile + broadband): ~MYR 165. Competitive mobile market drives affordable plans. Celcom, Maxis, Digi merged (CelcomDigi) creating dominant player.
Singapore household monthly telecom (mobile + fibre broadband): ~SGD 145. Fibre broadband ~SGD 30-60/month. Mobile plans SGD 20-70. Singtel, StarHub, M1 are main operators.
Indonesian household monthly telecom (mobile data): ~IDR 180,000 (~USD 11). Data is cheapest in Southeast Asia. Telkomsel, Indosat, XL Axiata are main operators. Average data usage: 12GB/month.
Australian household monthly telecom (mobile + NBN broadband): ~AUD 195. NBN average plan: AUD 70-110/month. Mobile: AUD 30-100. Telstra premium, Optus and TPG alternatives.
Italian household monthly telecom (mobile + broadband): ~EUR 68. Among cheapest mobile plans in EU (TIM, Vodafone, Wind3, Iliad compete aggressively). FTTH fiber rollout ongoing.

dataPoints.unit: percent of low income households receiving BPNT
dataPoints.context: ~40% of Indonesian low-income households receive BPNT (non-cash food aid) vouchers worth IDR 200,000-300,000/month for rice, eggs, and protein. Critical spending supplement for bottom 40%.
dataPoints.source: Ministry of Social Affairs Indonesia / TNP2K 2023

dataPoints.context: Malaysia Bantuan Rakyat 1Malaysia (BR1M/BSH/Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah): B40 households receive MYR 1,500+/year in cash transfers. Critical income supplement affecting spending patterns of bottom 40%.
Australia JobSeeker (unemployment benefit): AUD 762.70/fortnight (~AUD 1,525/month) in 2023. Below poverty line by many measures. Significant portion of household budget for recipients.
Singapore ComCare short-term assistance: typically SGD 300-700/month for needy households. GST vouchers (cash + MediSave) supplement low-income spending. SG's targeted social safety net.

Italy Reddito di Cittadinanza (citizen's income): avg EUR 550/month for eligible households in 2022-2023. Abolished Jan 2024 and replaced with more targeted support. 1.1 million households received it.
Indonesia household debt to GDP: 17.2% in 2022 — relatively low. But paylater (BNPL) debt growing rapidly especially among urban youth. OJK monitoring rising unsecured consumer credit risk.
dataPoints.source: IMF Global Debt Database / OJK Indonesia 2022

dataPoints.context: Australia household debt to GDP: 119% in 2022 — 4th highest globally (after Switzerland, Norway, Denmark). Driven almost entirely by housing. Highly sensitive to interest rate changes.
Singapore household debt to GDP: 68.4% in 2022. Mostly housing loans (mortgages). Low NPL ratio (0.2%) reflects strict TDSR/MSR lending framework. Debt manageable against high income base.
Malaysia household debt to GDP: 84.5% in 2022 — highest in Southeast Asia. Housing, car loans, and PTPTN dominate. Bank Negara tracks carefully as key macroprudential risk.
dataPoints.source: Bank Negara Malaysia Financial Stability Report 2022

dataPoints.context: Italy household debt to GDP: 41% in 2022 — significantly below EU average of 57%. Italians are culturally debt-averse. However, 26% of households hold debt, mostly mortgages.
dataPoints.source: Banca d'Italia / ECB Statistical Data Warehouse 2022

dataPoints.context: Shopee holds ~58% of Malaysia's e-commerce market vs Lazada ~25% (2023). Shopee's gamification, live streaming, and Hari Raya events dominate. TikTok Shop emerging as third player.
Indonesia e-commerce: Shopee ~36% GMV share, Tokopedia ~29%, Lazada ~15% in 2022. After TikTok-Tokopedia merger (Dec 2023), combined platform challenges Shopee dominance.
